68953-aspects-of-nature-in-different-lan.title: Scientific Elucidations.
68953-aspects-of-nature-in-different-lan.creator: Alexander Von Humboldt.
68953-aspects-of-nature-in-different-lan.description: A book by Alexander Von Humboldt.. found butterflies and other winged insects, borne by ascending currents of air to those almost unapproachable solitudes, which man, led by a restless curiosity or unappeasable thirst of knowledge, treads with adventurous but cautious steps: like him strangers in those elevated regions, their presence shows us that the more flexible organization of animal creation can subsist far beyond the limits at which vegetation ceases.

arxiv-2012-07528.title: Disentangling Homophemes in Lip Reading using Perplexity Analysis
arxiv-2012-07528.creator: Souheil Fenghour, Daqing Chen, Perry Xiao, Kun Guo
arxiv-2012-07528.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Souheil Fenghour, Daqing Chen, Perry Xiao, Kun Guo. The performance of automated lip reading using visemes as a classification schema has achieved less success compared with the use of ASCII characters and words largely due to the problem of different words sharing identical visemes. The Generative Pre-Training transformer is an effective autoregressive language model used for many tasks in Natural Language Processing, including sentence prediction and text classification.

arxiv-2104-01588.title: PINNtomo: Seismic tomography using physics-informed neural networks
arxiv-2104-01588.creator: Umair bin Waheed, Tariq Alkhalifah, Ehsan Haghighat, Chao Song, Jean Virieux
arxiv-2104-01588.description: Abstract Seismic traveltime tomography using transmission data is widely used to image the Earth’s interior from global to local scales. In seismic imaging, it is used to obtain velocity models for subsequent depth-migration or full-waveform inversion. In addition, cross-hole tomography has been successfully applied for a variety of applications, including mineral exploration, reservoir monitoring, and CO 2 injection and sequestration.

arxiv-2109-03402.title: Mixup Decoding for Diverse Machine Translation
arxiv-2109-03402.creator: Jicheng Li, Pengzhi Gao, Xuanfu Wu, Yang Feng, Zhongjun He, Hua Wu,, Haifeng Wang
arxiv-2109-03402.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Jicheng Li, Pengzhi Gao, Xuanfu Wu, Yang Feng, Zhongjun He, Hua Wu,, Haifeng Wang. Diverse machine translation aims at generating various target language translations for a given source language sentence. To leverage the linear relationship in the sentence latent space introduced by the mixup training, we propose a novel method, MixDiversity , to generate different translations for the input sentence by linearly interpolating it with different sentence pairs sampled from the training corpus during decoding.

arxiv-2307-06467.title: Searching for Exploding Black Holes
arxiv-2307-06467.creator: and Dana Hennings
arxiv-2307-06467.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by and Dana Hennings. The observation of the final stages of the evaporation of a light black hole, which Hawking referred to as “black hole explosion”, would offer critical insights on quantum gravity and high-energy physics phenomena. Here, we explore, review, and revisit the observational features and rates expected for nearby, light, evaporating black holes, and we assess and compare the expected sensitivity of a broad range of observatories.

arxiv-2308-11477.title: An improved column-generation-based matheuristic for learning classification trees Journal: Computers and Operations Research
arxiv-2308-11477.creator: Krunal Kishor Patel, Guy Desaulniers, Andrea Lodi
arxiv-2308-11477.description: Abstract Decision trees are highly interpretable models for solving classification problems in machine learning (ML). The standard ML algorithms for training decision trees are fast but generate suboptimal trees in terms of accuracy. Other discrete optimization models in the literature address the optimality problem but only work well on relatively small datasets. Firat et al.

arxiv-2406-06854.title: Current-readout technique for ultra-high-rate experiments
arxiv-2406-06854.creator: Maki Wakata, Shoei Akamatsu, Takuhiro Fujiie, Taisei Furuyama, Lisa Hara, Yumi Ishikawa, Tadashi Ito, Takahiro Kikuchi, Tsutomu Mibe, Sachi Ozaki, Mitsuhiko Yokomizo, Jiro Murata
arxiv-2406-06854.description: Abstract This study developed a new current-readout technique capable of handling measurements with high count rates reaching 1 Gcps. By directly capturing the output current of a photomultiplier as a digitized waveform, we estimated event rates, overcoming the limitations imposed by pulse pileup constraints and deadtimes.

arxiv-2504-01302.title: GPU-Accelerated Gravitational Lensing & \& Dynamical ( GLaD ) Modeling for Cosmology and Galaxies
arxiv-2504-01302.creator: Han Wang, Sherry H. Suyu, Aymeric Galan, Aleksi Halkola, Michele Cappellari, Anowar J. Shajib, Miha Cernetic
arxiv-2504-01302.description: Abstract Time-delay distance measurements from strongly lensed quasars provide a robust and independent method for determining the Hubble constant ( H 0 H_{0} ). This approach offers a crucial cross-check against H 0 H_{0} measurements obtained from the standard distance ladder in the late universe and the cosmic microwave background in the early universe.

arxiv-2505-07569.title: Melting of Charge Density Waves in Low Dimensions
arxiv-2505-07569.creator: Jeremy M. Shen, Alex Stangel, Suk Hyun Sung, Nishkarsh Agarwal, Ismail El Baggari, Kai Sun, Robert Hovden
arxiv-2505-07569.description: Abstract Charge density waves (CDWs) are collective electronic states that can reshape and melt, even while confined within a rigid atomic crystal. In two dimensions, melting is predicted to be distinct, proceeding through partially ordered nematic and hexatic states that are neither liquid nor crystal.

arxiv-2511-10377.title: Development of the CEPC analog hadron calorimeter prototype
arxiv-2511-10377.creator: Yukun Shi, Anshun Zhou, Hao Liu, Jiechen Jiang, Yanyun Duan, Yunlong Zhang, Zhongtao Shen, Jianbei Liu, Boxiang Yu, Shu Li, Haijun Yang, Yong Liu, Liang Li, Zhen Wang, Siyuan Song, Dejing Du, Jiaxuan Wang, Junsong Zhang, Quan Ji
arxiv-2511-10377.description: Abstract The Circular Electron Positron Collider (CEPC) is a next-generation electron–positron collider proposed for the precise measurement of the properties of the Higgs boson. To emphasize boson separation and jet reconstruction, the baseline design of the CEPC detector was guided by the particle flow algorithm (PFA) concept. As one of the calorimeter options, the analogue hadron calorimeter (AHCAL) was proposed.

arxiv-2604-13694.title: Weight Patching: Toward Source-Level Mechanistic Localization in LLMs
arxiv-2604-13694.creator: Chenghao Sun, Chengsheng Zhang, Guanzheng Qin, Rui Dai, and Xinmei Tian

britannica-1911-roscoff.title: Roscoff (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-roscoff.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-roscoff.description: Article 'Roscoff' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 23), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. France, in the department of Finistère, on the English Channel, 171 2 m. (1906) town, 1984; commune, 5054. Roscoff, separated from the Ile de Batz by a narrow channel, has a tidal port used by fishing and coasting vessels. Many of the inhabitants are engaged in the cultivation of early vegetables, to the growth of which the mild climate and fertile soil is eminently favourable.

pmc-12607288.title: A video-based educational intervention to improve vaccine acceptance for Schistosomiasis japonicum: A pre–post study using the 5C model in rural China
pmc-12607288.creator: Qianxu Yang, Jue Wang, Chunhong Du, Hai Yen Lee, Li Ping Wong
pmc-12607288.description: This study evaluated a video intervention to enhance knowledge of Schistosoma japonicum (SK) and general vaccines (GK) and examined how these factors influenced acceptance of a hypothetical Schistosoma japonicum vaccine via the 5C pathways (confidence, complacency, constraints, calculation, and collective responsibility). A single-arm pre – post study was conducted in Eryuan, China (2024).

pmc-12775534.title: Design framework and optimization of portable biomedical waste decomposition systems using ANN and MOPSO
pmc-12775534.creator: Naresh N Bhaiswar, Sushant S Satputaley, Sandeep M Kadam, P Dinesha, Sooraj Mohan
pmc-12775534.description: Biomedical waste (BMW) incineration requires accurate prediction of energy demand and efficiency due to its heterogeneous composition. In this study, material and energy balance calculations were combined with design of experiments (DOE), analysis of variance (ANOVA), artificial neural network (ANN) modeling, and multi-objective particle swarm optimization (MOPSO).

pmc-13237093.title: Multi-scale fractures and faults in tight reservoirs: from characterization to engineering applications
pmc-13237093.creator: Hu Li, Qingchao Li
pmc-13237093.description: Multi-scale fractures and fault systems in tight reservoirs are key controls on hydrocarbon accumulation and migration. They also provide the geological basis for effective hydraulic fracturing. The seven papers in this collection address cutting-edge topics. These include high-precision fracture and fault characterization, geomechanical response mechanisms, and natural–hydraulic fracture coupling.

pmc-13357117.title: Machine learning integration of routine inflammatory biomarkers for predicting remote punctate ischemic lesions following intracerebral hemorrhage: a single-center retrospective study
pmc-13357117.creator: Yibo Dong, Longyun Yi, Hongbo Tu
pmc-13357117.description: BackgroundRemote Punctate Ischemic Lesions (RPIL) occurring during the acute phase of intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) represent a paradox of “ischemia within hemorrhage” that is associated with worse functional outcome. While the concept of “thrombo-inflammation” is gaining traction, the predictive utility of novel biomarkers like the Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index (SII) combined with advanced machine learning (ML) remains uncharacterized.
